title: Does the coin stay on the record? At 45 rpm it stays; at 78 rpm it is off the rim in 0.18 s
description:
Does the coin stay on the record? The same record twice, seen from above: a 30 cm record (radius 15 cm) turns at a steady speed, clockwise, flush with a still deck around it (a lazy susan: the deck beyond the rim does not turn). A coin (a point mass for the physics, drawn 2.4 cm across; its mass cancels) sits 10 cm from the centre, held down by a fingertip so it moves with the record; at the release the fingertip lifts and friction alone must hold the coin. Friction mu = 0.3 between the coin and the record and the same on the deck, the same at rest and sliding, a chosen value for a coin on vinyl (the limit scales with sqrt(mu)); g = 9.807 m/s^2. Top panel 45 rpm (omega 4.7124 rad/s), bottom panel 78 rpm (omega 8.1681 rad/s). The coin rides along while the grip it needs, omega^2 r / g, is at most mu; the limit at radius r is omega* = sqrt(mu g / r), and a speed omega holds a coin out to mu g / omega^2. A sliding coin is integrated in the deck frame by RK4 at dt = 1e-05 s: its acceleration is mu g opposite to its velocity relative to the record surface under it (toward the centre at the release, when that velocity is zero); the rim crossing is located by bisection inside the step and checked by a half-step rerun. Past the rim the coin skids straight on the still deck at mu g: distance v^2 / (2 mu g), time v / (mu g). Shown at 1/10 speed; the run repeats every 10 s of video, 4 runs in 40 s. Deterministic, no seed.

Measured:
- the limit at 10 cm: omega* = sqrt(mu g / r) = 5.4241 rad/s = 51.80 rpm
- 45 rpm: the coin needs 0.2264 of grip against 0.30 available (margin 0.0736): it stays and rides round with the record; 45 rpm holds a coin out to mu g / omega^2 = 13.25 cm; it needs 51.80 rpm to move a coin at 10 cm, 6.80 rpm more
- 78 rpm: the coin needs 0.6803 of grip, 2.27 times what it has: it slides; 78 rpm would hold a coin only out to 4.41 cm (inside the label)
- 78 rpm slide (RK4): the coin reaches the rim 0.1797 s after the release, 69.2 degrees round the centre in the deck frame from where it started, moving at 0.8758 m/s (0.689 m/s relative to the record surface) while the record turned 84.1 degrees, so the coin lags the record by 14.8 degrees at the rim; under one fifth of a second; its exit velocity points 125.9 degrees from its starting radius
- slide table (time after the release, radius, angle round, speed): 50 ms 10.46 cm, 22.9 degrees, 0.822 m/s; 100 ms 11.74 cm, 43.3 degrees, 0.836 m/s; 150 ms 13.64 cm, 60.5 degrees, 0.858 m/s; 179.7 ms 15.00 cm, 69.2 degrees, 0.876 m/s
- skid on the still deck: v^2 / (2 mu g) = 13.0 cm in v / (mu g) = 0.298 s; the coin is at rest 0.477 s after the release, 28.0 cm from the record's centre
- 33 1/3 rpm needs 0.1242 of grip and holds a coin out to 24.15 cm
- 52 rpm (just over the limit) needs 0.3024: off the rim at 0.9514 s, 289.7 degrees round, at 0.7309 m/s while the record turned 296.8 degrees; skid 9.1 cm in 0.248 s
- 60 rpm needs 0.4026: off the rim at 0.3199 s, 103.2 degrees round, at 0.7598 m/s while the record turned 115.2 degrees; skid 9.8 cm in 0.258 s
- 100 rpm needs 1.1182: off the rim at 0.1241 s, 58.9 degrees round, at 1.0737 m/s while the record turned 74.5 degrees; skid 19.6 cm in 0.365 s
- a coin at the rim itself (15 cm) slides above 42.29 rpm; grip 0.2 at 10 cm: the limit is 42.29 rpm (45 and 78 rpm both slide); grip 0.5: 66.87 rpm (45 rpm holds, 78 rpm slides)
- checks: the half-step rerun (dt = 5e-06 s) moves the exit time by -7.4e-15 s; the run from angle 0 agrees within -1.0e-15 s; in the record's frame the coin starts outward at omega^2 r - mu g = 3.7298 m/s^2, so after 10 ms it is 0.0186 cm out, and RK4 gives 0.0186 cm; the relative speed after the first step stays above 3.73e-05 m/s, so the friction direction is always defined

Why: to go round in a circle the coin must be pulled toward the centre, and on a flat record only friction can do that. The pull it needs grows with the square of the turning speed: omega^2 r / g of its weight. At 45 rpm that is 0.23 of the weight, under the 0.30 the grip can give, so the coin rides round for ever. At 78 rpm it is 0.68, more than twice the grip, so the coin slips at once: friction now acts against its motion relative to the record, the coin falls behind the turn and drifts outward on a spiral, and 0.18 s after the fingertip lifts it is over the rim, moving at 0.88 m/s. On the still deck the same friction stops it in 13 cm.
